ModMetaData.name: Entertaining Ideas
ModMetaData.author: kanid99
ModMetaData.description:
Thirteen new recreation ideas (seventeen buildings), spread across the tech ladder, so a colony has something worth doing whether it is chewing pemmican in a hide tent or running an archotech lounge.
- Knucklebone mat (neolithic) - the thinking game a tribe can build on day one. Cast bones, argue, gamble. - Soaking tub (medieval) - a wood-fired barrel colonists get into. Warms the room, steams while the firebox is lit, and hides whoever is in it below the waterline. An electric version follows at industrial tech for anyone tired of hauling logs. Either way a tub holds one soak and somebody has to carry water out to it between uses - unless Dubs Bad Hygiene is installed and you run a pipe to it, in which case it fills itself. - Skittles lane (medieval) - five tiles of board and nine pins. Roll from the near end; the pins scatter when the ball arrives. - Shadow lantern theater (medieval) - a lamp, a linen screen, and a drum the flame turns by itself. The shadows walk whether or not anyone is watching, and a whole room can sit and watch them. - Pinball machines (industrial and up) - four themed tables on one 1x3 cabinet frame: the standard machine, the chemfuel-flashpot boomalope blitz, the solid-state mech rampage, and the archotech dreamtable that projects a ball you cannot miss. - Cocktail arcade table (industrial) - a face-up screen under glass with a joystick at each of two seats. The maze game runs while someone is playing it. - Aquarium (industrial) - fish that swim whether or not anyone is watching, and a lot of beauty. - Karaoke machine (industrial) - a crowd of up to five, and practice at handling other people. A turn at the microphone builds artistic and social skill. The singer has a good time no matter what; everyone else in the room makes up their own mind, based on whether the singer can actually hold a tune, what they think of them personally, and whether they were ever going to enjoy this. Being well liked covers for being terrible. - Massage chair (industrial) - colonists sit in it, not beside it. Rollers work up the backrest while it runs. - Hologame pod (spacer) - a board of light that tunes itself just past your ability. Trains intellectual. - Vista panel (spacer) - a 3x1 wall display showing somewhere with a horizon in it, running on the local clock: grey dawn, daylight, a long sunset, then stars. It lights the room to match, and colonists in that room hold off cabin fever for longer. - Gravball court (ultratech) - a 3x3 court with the ball held in a lazy orbit, played from the edges by up to four colonists. - Dreamloop holotheater (ultratech) - point it at a wall within six tiles and it throws a moving picture onto that wall. A whole room can watch, bedridden colonists included.
Includes a small assembly for the animated screens, the wall projection, the sit-in furniture, the vista panel and the karaoke crowd, built separately for 1.5 and 1.6 because 1.6 changed the joy-tick API. No new research either - everything gates on projects the game already has, so the tree gains seventeen buildings and not one extra node. No Harmony and no mod dependencies. If Dubs Bad Hygiene happens to be installed, the aquarium plumbs into its water network and the tubs join its hydrotherapy category; without it, nothing changes.
